## Approved Spec
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-01-due-date-design.md`

# Design: Due date for todos (Ticket #1)

Ticket: #1 "Fälligkeitsdatum für Todos" — todos get a due date so overdue items are
visible, in the API and in the list page.

## Intent and why
The list and the API should show which todos are overdue, so what is due soon or
already past gets attention. Due dates are set through the JSON API; the list page
only displays them.

## Goals
- `Todo` carries an optional, date-only due date (`DateOnly? DueDate`), serialized as
  `"dueDate": "YYYY-MM-DD"` (`null` when absent). No time component.
- Overdue rule: a todo is overdue iff it is **not done**, **has a due date**, and that
  date is **before today (UTC)**. A todo without a due date is never overdue.
- The API exposes the rule: every todo response includes a computed `"overdue"` flag,
  and `GET /todos?overdue=true` (or `=false`) filters the list by it.
- A due date can be set, changed, **and removed** again: `PATCH` with `"dueDate": null`
  clears the date; omitting the field leaves it unchanged (existing PATCH convention).
- Invalid due dates — wrong format (e.g. `"30.02.2026"`, `"next Friday"`) or an
  impossible calendar date (e.g. `"2026-02-30"`) — are rejected with HTTP 400
  `{"error": "..."}` like other malformed bodies.
- The list page shows each todo's due date; an overdue todo is marked with the word
  **„überfällig"**. A "nur überfällige" control on the page shows only overdue todos.
- Agreed scope (checks): `dotnet test` (store, API, page tests) **plus** the agent tests
  the changed flows end to end in the running app with Playwright (API filter, page
  marking, page "nur überfällige" control), per the AGENTS.md end-to-end section;
  screenshots go outside the repo.

## Non-goals
- No due-date input in the UI; the page stays read-only.
- No time-of-day, no time zones beyond "today in UTC".
- No sorting or grouping by due date.
- PATCH keeps its "absent = unchanged" convention for `title`/`done`; for `dueDate`
  an explicit `null` means "clear" (tri-state, see below).

## Constraints
- No new NuGet packages.
- Validation errors stay `System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations.ValidationException`,
  mapped to HTTP 400 `{"error": "..."}` in `Program.cs`. Malformed request bodies
  (including unparsable/invalid due dates) already surface as `BadHttpRequestException`
  and map to the same 400 shape; the new date parsing must throw `JsonException` so it
  lands there too.
- TDD: failing test in `tests/` first.
- Every UI element tests rely on carries a `data-testid`.

## Approaches
- **A (chosen):** `DueDate` plus a computed `Overdue` property on the `Todo` record —
  one source of truth for the rule; the API serializes `overdue` into JSON for free
  and the page sees it over the Blazor circuit.
- **B (rejected):** computed `overdue` only in an API response DTO, page computes it
  separately — two definitions of the rule, drift risk, plus mapping code.
- **C (rejected):** persist an `overdue` flag — goes stale at midnight UTC and would
  need a background job.

## Decisions agreed with the human
- Due date is optional and date-only (`DateOnly?`), no time.
- Overdue = not done AND due date before today (UTC); never overdue without a date.
- The API is filterable via `?overdue=true|false`.
- A due date can be removed again: `PATCH {"dueDate": null}` clears it; omitting the
  field keeps it (the PATCH record needs a tri-state for `dueDate` — absent vs.
  explicit null).
- Invalid due dates (wrong format or impossible date such as Feb 30) are rejected
  with HTTP 400 `{"error": "..."}`.
- The page marks an overdue todo with the word „überfällig" and has a
  "nur überfällige" control that lists only overdue todos.
- The agent tests end to end itself (Playwright in the running app).

## Left to the builder
- The tri-state mechanism for `TodoPatch.DueDate` (e.g. a small wrapper type with a
  `System.Text.Json` converter that turns an explicit JSON `null` into "clear" and
  throws `JsonException` for invalid date strings so they map to 400).
- Filtering by the shared `Overdue` rule for both `GET /todos?overdue=...` and the
  page's "nur überfällige" control (store method or in-place LINQ — one rule).
- Exact markup/styling of the due date, the „überfällig" marker, and the
  "nur überfällige" control, plus the new `data-testid`s (planned: `todo-due-date`,
  `todo-overdue`, `overdue-only-filter`).
- JSON shape details: camelCase `dueDate` / `overdue`, property order follows the
  record declaration.
- Test updates for the new JSON fields in existing assertions.

## Implementation Summary

## Implementation Summary

**Approach** — Todos carry an optional, date-only due date. `Todo` gained `DateOnly? DueDate` and a computed `Overdue` property (`!Done && DueDate < today UTC`) — one rule shared by the JSON API and the list page. `TodoPatch` carries the due date as a tri-state `DueDatePatch` (+ System.Text.Json converter), so `PATCH {"dueDate": null}` clears the date while an omitted field keeps it. `TodoStore.List(bool? overdue)` does the filtering; `GET /todos?overdue=true|false` and the page's "nur überfällige" checkbox both call it. The page shows each due date (`todo-due-date`), marks overdue todos with "überfällig" (`todo-overdue`), and offers the `overdue-only-filter` checkbox. Invalid dates (wrong format or impossible dates like 2026-02-30) throw `JsonException` and map to HTTP 400 `{"error": "..."}` via the existing middleware.

**Consequences** — Todo JSON responses now include `"dueDate"` and `"overdue"` (camelCase; order: id, title, done, dueDate, overdue), and `GET /todos` accepts `?overdue=true|false`. Additive only: the due date is optional, no new NuGet packages, existing clients keep working.

**Possible side effects** — `overdue` is computed at read time from the UTC date, so it flips at midnight UTC without any write; record equality is unchanged (the computed property is not positional).

**Watch when testing** — Boundaries: due today is not overdue, a done todo is never overdue, no date is never overdue; PATCH `null` clears vs. omitted keeps; 400 on `"2026-02-30"` and on `?overdue=banana`. End-to-end status: tested by the agent in the running app on http://localhost:3000 — API via curl (create/filter/400s/clear), page via Playwright (marking + "nur überfällige" toggle; screenshots /tmp/e2e-list.png, /tmp/e2e-overdue-only.png). `dotnet test`: 19/19 green.
